mainTopic: נבואה after the חורבן (חכמים, שוטים, תינוקות), sayings on the root נבב, and dividing an estate: joined shares for a בכור or יבם, and כופין על מדת סדום.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a proof that the חכמים still have a kind of נבואה after the חורבן. רב אשי rejects the proof from matching רבי עקיבא בר יוסף, since the two might share a מזל. He proves it instead from a חכם whose words match a הלכה למשה מסיני and who gives a reason for them. רבי יוחנן then teaches that נבואה also went to שוטים and תינוקות. Two stories show this: a שוטה's words lead to מר בר רב אשי becoming ראש מתיבתא, and רב חסדא's young daughter says she will marry both רבא and רמי בר חמא. Next come teachings on the root נבב: hunger splits a person's mind, and wine opens a closed mind. The גמרא then returns to dividing an estate. A בכור gets his two shares side by side, and אביי and רבא argue whether a יבם does too. Last, three cases ask when the court forces brothers to give a share next to a brother's own land under כופין על מדת סדום, and each time the הלכה follows רב יוסף.

steps.title: Finishing the proof: the same idea appears in the name of רבי עקיבא בר יוסף
steps.stepSummary: The last words of a proof from the previous lines. A great חכם says something, and the same idea is said in the name of רבי עקיבא בר יוסף.
steps.simpleTranslation: [A great man says something, and it is then said] in the name of רבי עקיבא בר יוסף, just like his words.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a proof it began just before this section. The proof claims that the חכמים still have some נבואה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that a later חכם is not on רבי עקיבא's level. If he still says exactly what רבי עקיבא said, he must have had help from heaven. The next step will question this proof.
steps.confusionAlert: This line starts in the middle of a sentence. The beginning ("תדע, דאמר גברא רבה מילתא ומתאמרא") came just before this section.

phrases.aramaic: מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא בַּר יוֹסֵף כְּווֹתֵיהּ.
phrases.english: in the name of Rabbi Akiva bar Yosef, in line with his statement.
phrases.notes: The start of this sentence came just before: a great man says something, and then the same thing is said in רבי עקיבא's name.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא בַּר יוֹסֵף כְּווֹתֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a proof begun before this section.
steps.raayaObject: That the חכמים still receive a form of נבואה after the חורבן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A later חכם's statement matches what רבי עקיבא בר יוסף said.

steps.title: רב אשי rejects the proof: maybe they share the same מזל
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the proof is weak. The later חכם may have been born under the same מזל as רבי עקיבא, so on this point he thinks the same way.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: What is the difficulty? Perhaps on this matter he shares the same מזל as רבי עקיבא!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי pushes back on the proof from step 1. Matching רבי עקיבא does not have to come from נבואה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two people born under the same מזל can naturally think alike on a certain matter. That gives a normal explanation for the match. So the proof from רבי עקיבא does not show נבואה.

keyTerms.meaning: Sharing his מזל, born under the same sign

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: And what is the difficulty?

phrases.aramaic: דִּלְמָא לְהָא מִילְּתָא בַּר מַזָּלֵיהּ הוּא!
phrases.english: Perhaps for this matter he is a son of his constellation!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof given in step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from רבי עקיבא, not the idea that חכמים have נבואה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A shared מזל can explain the matching idea without any נבואה.

steps.title: רב אשי's better proof: a חכם's words match a הלכה למשה מסיני
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי offers his own proof. A great חכם says something, and later it turns out to match a הלכה למשה מסיני.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אשי said: Know it is so, since a great man says something, and a הלכה למשה מסיני is then quoted that matches it.
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected the first proof, רב אשי gives a stronger one for the same idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A shared מזל can explain matching another person. It cannot explain matching a law that came straight from heaven to משה. Matching a הלכה למשה מסיני therefore points to help from heaven.

keyTerms.meaning: Know that it is so (introduces a proof)
A great man, a great חכם
A law given orally to משה at סיני

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Ashi said: Know that it is so,
since a great man says something,
and a law given to Moses at Sinai is then stated in line with him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the proof that was rejected in step 2.
steps.raayaObject: That the חכמים still receive a form of נבואה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A חכם's statement matches a הלכה למשה מסיני.

steps.title: Challenge: maybe he got it right by luck, like a blind man finding a skylight
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the חכם just guessed right, the way a blind man might happen to find an opening in the roof.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps it is like a blind man who finds a skylight!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב אשי's proof by suggesting the match happened by chance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A blind man cannot aim for the skylight. If he gets through it, that was luck. In the same way, the חכם may have stumbled onto the right answer without any help from heaven.

keyTerms.meaning: A skylight, an opening in the roof

phrases.english: But perhaps it is like a blind man through a skylight!
phrases.notes: A blind man can't find the opening on purpose. If he gets through, it's pure luck.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the proof from step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's proof from the הלכה למשה מסיני.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The match could be a lucky guess, so it does not prove נבואה.

steps.title: Answer: he gives a reason, so it is not luck
steps.stepSummary: The חכם explains why his ruling is right. Someone who gives a real reason did not guess.
steps.simpleTranslation: But doesn't he give a reason?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge in step 4 and saves רב אשי's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A lucky guesser cannot explain his answer. The חכם gives a טעם, which shows he truly understands the matter. So his match with the הלכה למשה מסיני shows guidance from heaven, not chance.
steps.whatToRemember: רב אשי's proof stands: a חכם who reaches a הלכה למשה מסיני and explains it with a reason shows that חכמים still have a kind of נבואה.

phrases.english: But does he not give a reason?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Pointing to a detail that rules out the challenge.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חכם may have guessed right by chance.
steps.terutzMaskana: He gives a reason, which shows real understanding, so the match is not luck.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: after the חורבן, נבואה went to שוטים and תינוקות
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that once the בית המקדש was destroyed, נבואה was taken from the נביאים and given to fools and children.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: From the day the בית המקדש was destroyed, נבואה was taken from the נביאים and given to fools and children.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement opens a related topic: another group that received a kind of נבואה after the חורבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא said נבואה moved to the חכמים. רבי יוחנן adds that it also showed up through שוטים and תינוקות. The גמרא will next explain what this means.

keyTerms.meaning: Fools, people not in their right mind

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
From the day that the Temple was destroyed,
prophecy was taken from the prophets
and given to fools and to children.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מִיּוֹם שֶׁחָרַב בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A related new teaching about where נבואה went after the חורבן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the חורבן, נבואה is found through שוטים and תינוקות.

steps.title: How was נבואה given to fools?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for an example of נבואה coming through a שוטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: To fools: what does this mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next move. It asks for an example, and a story will follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is hard to picture a שוטה having נבואה. The גמרא wants a real case that shows how it works.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? / What does it mean?

phrases.english: To fools: what is this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for an example of part of רבי יוחנן's statement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A real example of נבואה coming through a שוטה.

steps.title: A fool in מחוזא announces the next ראש מתיבתא
steps.stepSummary: מר בר רב אשי hears a שוטה in the street of מחוזא say that the new head of the ישיבה in מתא מחסיא signs his name "טביומי."
steps.simpleTranslation: Like the case of מר בר רב אשי, who was standing in the street of מחוזא. He heard a certain fool saying: The head of the ישיבה who will be appointed in מתא מחסיא signs "טביומי."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a story. A שוטה says something that turns out to be a true prediction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fool's words sound random, but they hold a real hint about the future. The next step shows how מר בר רב אשי understood them.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הָא דְּמָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי –
phrases.english: Like this case of Mar bar Rav Ashi,
who was standing in the street of Meḥoza,
he heard a certain fool who was saying:
The head of the yeshiva who will be appointed in Mata Meḥasya
signs "Tavyumei."

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הָא דְּמָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the story that answers the question in step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A שוטה foretold who would become ראש מתיבתא in מתא מחסיא.

steps.title: מר בר רב אשי realizes it is him and goes
steps.stepSummary: מר בר רב אשי knows he is the only חכם who signs "טביומי." He takes this as a sign that his moment has come and travels there. By the time he arrives, the רבנן have already decided to appoint רב אחא מדפתי.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: Who among the רבנן signs "טביומי"? Me. Learn from this that the moment is standing ready for me. He got up and came. By the time he came, the רבנן had decided to seat רב אחא מדפתי as head.
steps.whatsHappening: The story goes on. מר בר רב אשי understands the fool's words and acts on them, but he seems to have come too late.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fool's words fit only one person, so מר בר רב אשי treats them as a sign from heaven. The other candidate, רב אחא מדפתי, makes it look as if the prediction might fail. That sets up the ending.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it, we can conclude
To seat him at the head, to appoint him leader

phrases.english: He said: Who among the Sages signs "Tavyumei"? Me.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ לְדִידִי קָיְימָא לִי שַׁעְתָּא.
phrases.english: Conclude from it that the hour is standing ready for me.
He arose and came.
By the time he came, the Sages had decided
to seat Rav Aḥa of Difti at the head.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story from step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מר בר רב אשי sees that the fool's words point to him and acts on them.

steps.title: The pairs of רבנן reach ten, and מר בר רב אשי gives the דרשה
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן send pairs of חכמים to consult him, and he keeps each pair with him until ten are gathered. Then he opens and gives the דרשה, because one does not open a lecture at a כלה with fewer than ten. The fool's prediction comes true.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once they heard he had come, they sent a pair of רבנן to consult with him. He kept them. They sent another pair, and he kept them with him too, until there were ten. Once there were ten, he opened, taught, and expounded, because one does not open a lecture at a כלה with fewer than ten.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends. מר בר רב אשי waits for ten people, gives the דרשה, and the fool's prediction comes true.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He held back the messengers on purpose, because a דרשה at a כלה needs at least ten people. By teaching in front of them, he shows he is fit to lead the ישיבה. This completes the example of נבואה through a שוטה.

keyTerms.meaning: He held him back, kept him
The large gatherings for Torah learning

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's teaching is shown in action: a שוטה's random-sounding words correctly foretold that מר בר רב אשי would become ראש מתיבתא in מתא מחסיא.
steps.whyThisMatters: The last line also teaches a practical rule: a public דרשה at a כלה is not opened with fewer than ten people.

phrases.english: As soon as they heard that he had come,

phrases.aramaic: שַׁדּוּר זוּגָא דְּרַבָּנַן לְגַבֵּיהּ לְאִימְּלוֹכֵי בֵּיהּ.
phrases.english: they sent a pair of Sages to him to consult with him.
He detained them.
They again sent another pair of Sages,
and he detained them with him.
Until they filled up a group of ten.
Once they filled up a group of ten,
he opened, taught, and expounded.

phrases.aramaic: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין פּוֹתְחִין בְּכַלָּה פָּחוֹת מֵעֲשָׂרָה.
phrases.english: Because one does not open a lecture at a kalla with fewer than ten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the story and shows the fool's prediction coming true.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The שוטה's words came true, which shows that after the חורבן a kind of נבואה can come through שוטים, as רבי יוחנן taught.

steps.title: רב אחא accepts that he was passed over
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא מדפתי, who lost the appointment, quotes a saying about himself: when luck turns against someone it does not quickly turn back, and when it is for someone it does not quickly turn away.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא applied this saying to himself: Whoever has bad things happen to him does not quickly have good things happen to him. And whoever has good things happen to him does not quickly have bad things happen to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The story of מר בר רב אשי ends with רב אחא's reaction. He accepts that the job went to someone else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אחא sees that his chance is gone, and that מר בר רב אשי's good fortune will last. His words close the story that showed the שוטה's prediction coming true.

keyTerms.meaning: He read (applied) a saying or verse to himself

steps.whatToRemember: The fool's prediction fully came true: מר בר רב אשי became head of the ישיבה, and רב אחא accepted that his turn had passed.

phrases.english: Rav Acha read about himself:
Anyone who is treated badly
phrases.notes: Literally, 'anyone they do bad to.' He means someone whose luck has turned against him.

phrases.english: will not quickly be treated well,
and anyone who is treated well
will not quickly be treated badly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the final reaction of the man who lost the appointment, closing the שוטה story.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The appointment of מר בר רב אשי is settled and will last, just as the שוטה said.

steps.title: What is an example of prophecy through children?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for an example of the second part of רבי יוחנן's teaching: נבואה given to children.
steps.simpleTranslation: And children: what is the example of that?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. It already showed נבואה through a fool, and now it asks for an example with children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said נבואה went to fools and to children. Step 7 asked about fools; this question asks about the other group, so the next step will tell a story.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? (asking for an example or explanation)

phrases.english: Children: what is it?
phrases.notes: He's going back to רבי יוחנן, who said נבואה was given to fools and children.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel to Step 7: after the fool example, the גמרא now asks about children.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A real case showing a child speaking words of נבואה.

steps.title: רב חסדא's young daughter says she wants both students
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא's little daughter sits on his lap while רבא and רמי בר חמא sit before him. He jokingly asks which one she wants, and she answers 'both.' רבא adds, 'and I will be last.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Like the case of רב חסדא's daughter. She was sitting on her father's lap, and רבא and רמי בר חמא were sitting in front of him. He asked her: Which of them do you want? She said: Both of them. רבא said: And I will be the last one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a story. A little girl says something that later turned out to be a true prediction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The child answered 'both', which sounds impossible for a marriage. The גמרא takes it as נבואה, because she later married both of them: first רמי בר חמא and, after he died, רבא. That is why רבא says 'I will be last.'

keyTerms.meaning: On her father's lap (literally, in his 'wings', the folds of his garment)

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not spell out the ending of the story. The point is that her childish answer 'both' came true, which is what makes it an example of נבואה through a child.

phrases.english: Like this case of Rav Chisda's daughter:
she was sitting on her father's lap,
and sitting in front of him were
Rava and Rami bar Chama.
He said to her: Which of them do you want?
She said to him: Both of them.
Rava said: And I will be last.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of Step 12 with a story.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A child's casual answer, 'both of them', turned out to be a true prediction of who she would marry.

steps.title: A hungry person has two hearts; after eating, one
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבדימי דמן חיפה teaches that before eating and drinking a person's mind is divided ('two hearts'), and afterward it is settled ('one heart').
steps.simpleTranslation: Rabbi Avdimi from Haifa said: Before a person eats and drinks, he has two hearts. After he eats and drinks, he has only one heart.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new teaching from רבי אבדימי דמן חיפה, who was quoted earlier about נבואה. He says hunger leaves a person unsettled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Two hearts' means a divided, distracted mind, because hunger pulls a person's attention away. Once he has eaten, his mind is whole and focused. The proof from a פסוק comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Two hearts: a divided, unsettled mind
One heart: a settled, focused mind

phrases.english: Rabbi Avdimi from Haifa said:
Before a person eats and drinks,
he has two hearts;
after he eats and drinks,
he has only one heart.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic, connected only because it brings another teaching of רבי אבדימי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hunger divides a person's mind; eating and drinking settle it.

steps.title: Proof from a פסוק that נבוב means hollow
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבדימי brings the פסוק 'איש נבוב ילבב' and shows from 'נבוב לחת', which the תרגום renders 'hollow with planks', that נבוב means empty, so an empty (hungry) man is 'two-hearted.'
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'A hollow man is two-hearted.' And it is written: 'hollow with planks', which we translate into Aramaic as 'hollow with boards.'
steps.whatsHappening: Here comes the proof for the teaching in the last step. It uses one פסוק for the idea and a second פסוק to explain the hard word נבוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ילבב is read as 'has two hearts.' To show that נבוב means hollow or empty, the גמרא points to the מזבח, described as נבוב לחת, which the תרגום translates as hollow. So an 'empty' person, one who has not eaten, is the one with two hearts.

keyTerms.meaning: Hollow, empty; here, a person with an empty stomach
Will be 'two-hearted', read from the doubled letter ב
And we translate it (in the Aramaic Targum)

phrases.english: As it is said: "A hollow man is two-hearted"
phrases.notes: איוב 11:12. The doubled ב in ילבב is heard as 'two hearts.'

phrases.english: and it is written: "hollow with planks"
and we translate it: "hollow with boards."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the scriptural source for רבי אבדימי's statement in Step 14.
steps.raayaObject: That a hungry (empty) person has a divided mind.
steps.raayaSupportSource: איוב 11:12, with the meaning of נבוב proven from שמות 27:8 and its Targum.

steps.title: Wine opens even a closed mind
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע teaches that for someone used to wine, even if his mind is sealed shut like a בתולה, wine opens it, based on 'ותירוש ינובב בתלות.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רב יהושע said: A person who is used to wine, even if his heart is closed up like a virgin, wine opens it. As it says: 'And new wine opens up the virgins.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another teaching that uses the same root word, נבב. This one is about wine opening up the mind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In זכריה the word ינובב comes from the same root as נבוב, 'hollow.' רב הונא reads it as 'makes an opening': wine clears out a closed mind so it can understand. The 'closed like a virgin' image comes from the word בתלות in the same פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: One who is used to drinking wine
Opens it up, makes it clear and sharp
Will open up, make hollow (same root as נבוב)

steps.whatToRemember: Both teachings play on the root נבב, 'hollow.' Food settles a mind that hunger divides, and wine opens a mind that is closed.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said:
One who is used to wine,
even if his heart is closed like a virgin,
phrases.notes: 'Heart' here means his mind and understanding.

phrases.english: wine opens it up,
as it is said: "And new wine opens up the virgins."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues working with the root נבב from Step 15, applying it to wine.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For one used to wine, wine opens even a closed mind to understanding.

steps.title: A firstborn's two portions are given side by side
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע states it is obvious that a בכור receives his extra portion and his regular portion as one joined parcel along a single boundary.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רב יהושע said: It is obvious that a firstborn's portion and his ordinary portion are given to him along one boundary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching about dividing an estate: a בכור's two shares are placed next to each other. This sets up the question that comes right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור inherits a double share: one extra 'firstborn portion' plus a regular share like his brothers. רב הונא says the brothers must give him both shares as one connected piece, not scattered. He calls this obvious, which prepares us for a case that is less obvious.

keyTerms.meaning: The extra share a firstborn inherits
An ordinary share, like every other brother gets
Boundary; the edge of a field

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said:
It is obvious: a firstborn's portion and an ordinary portion –
we give them to him along one boundary.
phrases.notes: He means the two shares sit next to each other, so together they make one field.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: פְּשִׁיטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same אמורא as step 16, but this is a new legal topic about dividing an estate.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בכור's firstborn share and ordinary share are given to him as one connected plot.

steps.title: What about a יבם?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a יבם, who inherits his dead brother's share along with his own, also gets both shares side by side.
steps.simpleTranslation: A יבם – what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: Having said the בכור case is obvious, the גמרא now asks about a יבם, who also ends up with two shares.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A יבם who marries his brother's widow takes his dead brother's share of their father's estate in addition to his own. The question is whether his two shares must also be joined like a בכור's, or whether that rule applies only to a real בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: A man who marries his brother's widow when the brother died without children

phrases.english: A yavam – what?
phrases.notes: He also inherits two shares: his own and his dead brother's. Must they be joined too?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the obvious rule of step 17 and asks whether it extends to a similar case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a יבם, like a בכור, receive his two shares along one boundary?

steps.title: אביי: a יבם is treated like a בכור
steps.stepSummary: אביי rules that the יבם is the same as the בכור, because the Torah calls the יבם a 'בכור'.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: This is the same as that. What is the reason? The Merciful One called him 'firstborn.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers that a יבם gets his two shares joined, exactly like a בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about יבום uses the word 'הבכור' for the brother who does יבום. אביי reads this as making the יבם like a בכור in every way, so the joined-boundary rule applies to him too.

keyTerms.meaning: It is the same; this case equals that case

phrases.english: Abaye said: this is that;
phrases.notes: He means the יבם's case is exactly like the בכור's case.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
The Merciful One called him "firstborn."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18 in the positive.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. The יבם gets his shares joined, since the Torah calls him בכור.

steps.title: רבא: a יבם inherits like a בכור but is not given joined portions
steps.stepSummary: רבא reads the פסוק 'והיה הבכור' as limited: the יבם is like a בכור in what he inherits, but not in how the estate is split.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The verse says, 'And it shall be, the firstborn' – his 'being' is like a firstborn, but his division is not like a firstborn.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא disagrees with אביי and says the יבם does not get his two shares joined.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא focuses on the word 'והיה' ('and it shall be'). He reads it as limiting the comparison: the יבם is like a בכור in actually receiving the extra share, but not in how the land is divided. So the brothers do not have to give him two shares side by side.

keyTerms.meaning: His 'being'; here, the fact that he inherits the share
His division; how the land is split for him

steps.confusionAlert: רבא does not say the יבם loses his brother's share. He still inherits it like a בכור. Only the joining of the two shares along one boundary is denied.

phrases.english: Rava said: the verse says:
"And it shall be, the firstborn" –
his being is like a firstborn,
phrases.notes: 'Being' plays on the word 'והיה.' He gets the share, just like a בכור does.

phrases.english: but his division is not like a firstborn.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר, אָמַר קְרָא: וְהָיָה הַבְּכוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to step 18's question, disagreeing with אביי in step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No. The יבם inherits like a בכור but does not get his shares joined.
steps.whatToRemember: אביי: a יבם is like a בכור in everything, so his shares are joined. רבא: like a בכור only in what he inherits, not in how the land is divided.

steps.title: A brother who owns neighboring land asks for his share next to it
steps.stepSummary: A man bought land bordering the family estate. When the brothers divided it, he asked for his share beside his land. רבה rules that the court forces the brothers to agree, to stop מדת סדום.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man bought land along the boundary of his family's estate. When they were dividing it, he said to them: Divide for me along my boundary. רבה said: In a case like this, we compel against מדת סדום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real case about dividing an estate and gives רבה's ruling: the brothers must give him the share next to his land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since all the shares are equal in value, it seems to make no difference to the brothers which share they get, while it really helps him to have his share next to his own land. Refusing a favor that costs you nothing is called מדת סדום, and רבה says the court can force people not to act that way.

keyTerms.meaning: The trait of Sodom: refusing a favor that costs you nothing

steps.whyThisMatters: This brings in the wider idea of כופין על מדת סדום, that a court can force a person to give up a right that does him no good when holding onto it only hurts someone else.

phrases.english: A certain man who bought land
along the boundary of his family's estate.
When they were dividing, he said to them:
Divide for me along my boundary.
Rabba said: in a case such as this –
we compel against the trait of Sodom.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא דִּזְבַן אַרְעָא אַמִּצְרָא דְּבֵי נְשֵׁיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from joining a בכור's or יבם's shares to a new case about getting a share next to land the heir already owns.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The brothers are forced to give him the share bordering his land, because refusing would be מדת סדום.

steps.title: רב יוסף: the brothers can value that piece more highly
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף objects that this is not מדת סדום, because the brothers can say the plot next to his land is worth more, like the famous fields of בר מריון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף objected: The brothers can say to him, We value it highly, like the property of the house of בר מריון!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף challenges רבה's ruling by showing that the brothers do lose something if they give in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה assumed the brothers lose nothing, since all the shares are equal. רב יוסף answers that the plot next to the brother's land is especially desirable, so the brothers can treat it as more valuable. Once refusing has a real reason, it is not מדת סדום and the court cannot force them.

keyTerms.meaning: A man known for very valuable property

phrases.english: Rav Yosef objected to it:
The brothers can say to him,
we assess it at a high value
like the property of the house of bar Maryon!
phrases.notes: Since you want this piece so much, it is worth more, like those famous fields.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבה's ruling in step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's ruling that the brothers are forced to give the bordering plot under כופין על מדת סדום.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: מדת סדום only applies when the one refusing loses nothing. Here the bordering plot is worth more, so the brothers lose something by giving it up.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רב יוסף
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules like רב יוסף: the brothers do not have to give him the plot next to his land.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is like רב יוסף.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the argument by ruling that the הלכה follows רב יוסף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the bordering plot has extra value, the brothers may refuse to give it to him, and the court does not force them. רבה's מדת סדום claim does not apply here.
steps.whatToRemember: A brother who owns land next to the estate cannot force his brothers to give him the share beside it, since that plot is worth more. The הלכה follows רב יוסף.

phrases.english: And the halacha is in accordance with Rav Yosef.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the dispute between רבה (step 21) and רב יוסף (step 22).
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The brothers can refuse to give the plot next to his own land, and the court does not force them.

steps.title: Two plots on two channels: רבה says the court forces the brothers
steps.stepSummary: Two inherited plots each sit by a different water channel. רבה rules that the court forces the other brother to give the plot next to the first brother's own field, to stop מדת סדום.
steps.simpleTranslation: If there are two plots of land by two water channels, רבה says: in a case like this, the court forces people not to act with מדת סדום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new version of the case from Step 21. This time the two inherited plots each sit by a different water channel, and רבה says the court still forces the brothers to give the brother the plot next to his own field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה holds that the two plots are basically equal. So refusing the brother the plot next to his field costs the other brother nothing, and that kind of refusal is מדת סדום. רבה is applying the same logic he used in Step 21 to a slightly different setup.

keyTerms.meaning: water channels used to water the fields
the behavior of Sodom: refusing someone a favor that costs you nothing

phrases.english: Two plots of land next to two water channels —
Rabba said:

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן זֶה – כּוֹפִין עַל מִדַּת סְדוֹם.
phrases.english: In a case like this, the court forces people not to act with the behavior of Sodom.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּרֵי אַרְעָתָא אַתְּרֵי נִגְרֵי – אָמַר רַבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the מדת סדום rule from Step 21 to a new case with two separate channels.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With two plots on two channels, the court forces the brothers to give the brother the plot next to his own field.

steps.title: רב יוסף objects: the two channels may not be equal
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף objects that this is not מדת סדום, because one channel may keep flowing while the other stops. That means the choice of plot really matters to the other brother.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף challenged this: sometimes this channel keeps flowing and that one does not!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף attacks רבה's ruling. He says the other brother has a real reason to want that specific plot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מדת סדום only applies when refusing costs you nothing. Two different channels may not be equally reliable: one might keep running and the other might dry up. So the plots are not truly equal, and the other brother's refusal is a fair concern, not cruelty.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef challenged it:
Sometimes this channel keeps flowing
and this one does not keep flowing!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבה's ruling in Step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's claim that the court forces the brothers in the two-channel case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The two plots are not truly equal, since one channel may dry up. So refusing is a real concern and not מדת סדום.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רב יוסף in the two-channel case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules like רב יוסף: with two separate channels, the court does not force the brothers.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה follows רב יוסף.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא decides the argument between רבה and רב יוסף about the two-channel case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the two channels may differ, the other brother has a fair reason to refuse. So the court does not force him to give up the plot.

phrases.english: And the halacha follows Rav Yosef.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the dispute in Steps 24-25.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: With two plots on two different channels, the court does not force the brothers.

steps.title: Two plots on one channel: רב יוסף says the court forces the brothers
steps.stepSummary: Now both plots sit on the same channel. רב יוסף himself rules that here the court does force the brothers, to stop מדת סדום.
steps.simpleTranslation: If there are two plots on one water channel, רב יוסף says: in a case like this, the court forces people not to act with מדת סדום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second case where both plots share one channel. This time רב יוסף agrees that the court forces the brothers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף's earlier objection was that two channels might not be equal. Here there is only one channel, so the water worry is gone and the plots really are equal. That makes refusing the brother the plot next to his field pure מדת סדום.

phrases.english: Two plots on one water channel —
Rav Yosef said:

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן זֶה – כּוֹפִין עַל מִדַּת סְדוֹם.
phrases.english: In a case like this, the court forces people not to act with the behavior of Sodom.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּרְתֵּי אַחַד נִגְרָא – אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a case without רב יוסף's water concern, where he agrees the court forces the brothers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With two plots on one channel, the court forces the brothers to give the brother the plot next to his own field.

steps.title: אביי objects: the other brother wants more sharecroppers around
steps.stepSummary: אביי objects that the other brother can say he wants more sharecroppers working near his field, so his refusal is not מדת סדום.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי challenged this: the other brother can say, 'I want there to be more sharecroppers.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רב יוסף's ruling. He offers a reason why the other brother might still want that specific plot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If one brother ends up with fields on both sides, more workers will be around. A brother whose field sits between them gets more people nearby watching his land. אביי says this is a real benefit, so refusing is not מדת סדום.

keyTerms.meaning: that I should increase, make more
sharecroppers, workers who farm a field for a share of the crop

phrases.english: Abaye challenged it:
The other brother can say:
I want the number of sharecroppers to increase!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's ruling in Step 27.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim that the court forces the brothers in the one-channel case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The other brother gains something from refusing (more sharecroppers nearby), so it is not a costless refusal and not מדת סדום.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רב יוסף: more sharecroppers is not a real reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules like רב יוסף, because having more sharecroppers around is not considered a real benefit. So the court forces the brothers in the one-channel case.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה follows רב יוסף, because having more sharecroppers is nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא decides the argument between אביי and רב יוסף and gives its reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא rejects אביי's reason: more sharecroppers is not a meaningful gain. Without a real reason to refuse, the refusal is מדת סדום, so the court forces it.

keyTerms.meaning: a real thing, a meaningful concern

steps.whatToRemember: The court forces the brothers only when refusing really costs them nothing. A plot next to the brother's own land is worth more, so the court does not force them. Two different channels may not be equal, so again it does not force them. With one shared channel the plots are equal, and the 'more sharecroppers' reason does not count, so here the court does force them. In all three cases the הלכה follows רב יוסף.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't be thrown off that רב יוסף 'wins' from opposite sides. In the first two cases (the land bordering his own, and the two channels) he objects to רבה's forcing. In the one-channel case he is the one who forces. His single principle is that a real reason to prefer one plot blocks forcing, but a weak reason does not.

phrases.english: And the halacha follows Rav Yosef;
having more sharecroppers is not a real concern.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהִלְכְתָא כְּרַב יוֹסֵף; אַפּוֹשֵׁי לָאו מִילְּתָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the dispute in Steps 27-28 and rejects אביי's reason.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: With two plots on one channel, the court forces the brothers, because wanting more sharecroppers is not a valid reason to refuse.
